The general form of a non-linear optimization problem can be expressed as follows:

\[
\min_{z \in \mathbb{R}^n} E(z) \quad \text{subject to} \quad h(z) = 0, \quad g(z) \leq 0, \quad z_{\text{low}} \leq z \leq z_{\text{upp}} \tag{15.1}
\]

where \(E(z)\) is the objective function to be minimized, \(h(z)\) represents equality constraints, and \(g(z)\) denotes inequality constraints.

1. **Convergence Properties**: The initial guess, denoted as \(z_0\), serves as the starting point for the iterative optimization algorithm.
